A16-8.label: Existentialist Film
A16-8.defn: An art-film character study whose engine is a crisis of meaning in the present tense — alienation, ennui, or a self disguised or doubled (La Dolce Vita, The Silence, Lost in Translation, The Passenger, The Double Life of Véronique). A life weighed up at its middle or end goes to the Midlife Crisis Film; a clinical inner state to A16-7; a quiet everyday portrait to A16-9.
A16-8.axis: by the shape of the crisis: alienation first, divided by era (the postwar modernist wave to 1979, its late-modernist continuation in the 1980s–90s, the contemporary festival film), then the ennui of the affluent, and double lives and masks last

new_leaves.label: Midlife Crisis Film
new_leaves.breadth: existential dramas of a life weighed up — at its middle, in old age, or reviewed whole from rise to fall
new_leaves.defn: A drama whose crisis of meaning comes from taking stock of a life already lived: the midlife crisis, the reckoning of old age, or a whole life reviewed in its rise and fall (Dodsworth, Save the Tiger, Husbands, Citizen Kane, Death of a Salesman, Youth, Gran Torino). Test: the film's engine is the review of a life's course rather than a present-tense alienation (A16-8) or a clinical breakdown (A16-7).
new_leaves.aliases: midlife-crisis drama; late-life drama; life-review film
new_leaves.axis: by where the life is weighed up: the whole life reviewed in its rise and fall first, then the crisis at midlife, and old age and last reckonings last

A16-22.label: Social Problem Film
A16-22.defn: A drama built to expose one named social ill of prejudice, violence or patriarchy — racism and caste, youth violence and its institutions, sexual violence and reproductive rights, the oppression of women (Gentleman's Agreement, Within Our Gates, Never Rarely Sometimes Always, Moolaadé). Addiction goes to the Addiction Drama; prostitution and trafficking to the Prostitution Film; diffuse working-class hardship to A16-19; the courtroom to A16-25.
A16-22.axis: by the social ill: race and caste first, then youth violence and reform schools, sexual violence and reproductive rights, and the oppression of women last

new_leaves.label: Addiction Drama
new_leaves.breadth: social-problem dramas of drink, drugs and gambling
new_leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is one person's or one milieu's addiction — to alcohol, drugs or gambling — followed through craving, collapse and (sometimes) recovery (The Lost Weekend, Days of Wine and Roses, The Man with the Golden Arm, Requiem for a Dream, The Gambler). Test: the addiction itself is the subject, not a backdrop to crime (A2) or a psychological portrait (A16-7).
new_leaves.aliases: drug film; alcoholism film; addiction film
new_leaves.axis: by the substance: drink first, then drugs, and gambling last

new_leaves.label: Prostitution Film
new_leaves.breadth: dramas of sex work, the fallen woman and trafficking
new_leaves.defn: A drama whose subject is prostitution as a social condition — the fallen woman of the silent and studio eras, the brothel and the red-light district, the street, and modern trafficking (Diary of a Lost Girl, Street of Shame, Nights of Cabiria, Mamma Roma, Lilya 4-Ever, Much Loved). Test: selling sex is the protagonist's situation and the film's subject; an erotic treatment goes to A15.
new_leaves.aliases: fallen-woman film; sex-work drama; trafficking drama
new_leaves.axis: by era, as the field divides it: the fallen-woman film of the silent and early sound eras, the postwar brothel and red-light film, then the modern sex-work and trafficking drama

A19-5.label: Diary Film
A19-5.defn: A first-person documentary whose subject is the filmmaker's own life as it is lived and recorded — the film diary, the home movie, the video or digital self-portrait, the chronicle of illness, exile or confinement (Reminiscences of a Journey to Lithuania, Sherman's March, Tarnation, Dear Diary, This Is Not a Film). A film that turns the camera on the filmmaker's parents, siblings or family history goes to the Family Documentary.
A19-5.axis: by the diary's form and occasion: home movies first, the New American Cinema film diary and the essayistic life-diary, auteurs' diaries and self-portraits, then diaries of illness, exile and political confinement, and the video and digital diary last
secs: Film Diaries of the New American Cinema & After

new_leaves.label: Family Documentary (Domestic Ethnography)
new_leaves.breadth: first-person documentaries about the filmmaker's own family
new_leaves.defn: A first-person documentary in which the filmmaker turns the camera on their own family — a parent, grandparent, sibling or child, or a family secret and history — and the film is about them rather than the filmmaker's own days (Sink or Swim, Nobody's Business, Stories We Tell, Dick Johnson Is Dead, The Flat, No Home Movie). Test: the family member or family past is the subject; the filmmaker's own life chronicled stays in the Diary Film.
new_leaves.aliases: domestic ethnography; family portrait documentary; autobiographical family documentary
new_leaves.axis: by whom the camera turns to: parents and grandparents first, then siblings, children and the household, and family secrets and histories last

A16-6.label: Melodrama
A16-6.defn: A drama in the melodramatic mode — heightened emotion, sacrifice and fate carried by music and mise-en-scène — whose sacrifice is made for a child or a family, or to illness (Stella Dallas, Imitation of Life, Written on the Wind, Dark Victory, All About My Mother). The melodrama of the fallen, desiring or self-sacrificing woman in love goes to the Woman's Film; realist family dramas to A16-3 to A16-5.
A16-6.axis: by the sacrifice at the core: maternal sacrifice first, then the family melodrama, the illness tearjerker, and Sirk's non-melodrama studio pictures last

new_leaves.label: Woman's Film
new_leaves.breadth: melodramas of the fallen, desiring or self-sacrificing woman, across national studio traditions
new_leaves.defn: A melodrama centred on a woman's desire, fall or sacrifice in love, marriage or work, made for and around a female star or a woman's point of view (The Cheat, Pandora's Box, Back Street, All That Heaven Allows, When a Woman Ascends the Stairs, Far from Heaven). Test: the heroine's own passion or fall is the engine; sacrifice for a child or a family stays in A16-6.
new_leaves.aliases: woman's picture; women's film; fallen-woman melodrama; josei eiga
new_leaves.axis: by era and national studio tradition: the silent vamp and fallen woman first, then the Hollywood woman's film, the European, Japanese, Chinese-Korean-Indian and Latin American traditions, and the modern revisionist woman's film last

A16-9.label: Slice of Life
A16-9.defn: A drama with no plot engine beyond a settled daily life observed — routines, rituals, small encounters and the passing days of people at home in their place (Paterson, Perfect Days, Café Lumière, The Scent of Green Papaya). A life adrift goes to the Drifter Film; a crisis of meaning to A16-8; a journey to A16-36.
A16-9.axis: by national and regional tradition, as festival everyday cinema is grouped: East Asia first (the Japanese, Korean, Chinese and Taiwanese quotidian film), then Western Europe, Eastern Europe and Central Asia, North America, Latin America, and the rest of the world last
secs: Eastern Europe, the Caucasus & Central Asia
Middle East, Africa, South & Southeast Asia, Oceania

new_leaves.label: Drifter Film
new_leaves.breadth: dramas of loners and drifters without settled place or purpose
new_leaves.defn: A drama of observed days whose protagonist is adrift — a loner, wanderer or young person between jobs, homes and attachments, followed without a plot engine (Wanda, Wendy and Lucy, Naked, Millennium Mambo, Morvern Callar, Old Joy). Test: the life is unsettled and the drift is the subject; a journey with a destination goes to A16-36, a settled daily routine stays in A16-9.
new_leaves.axis: by national and regional tradition: East Asia first, then Western Europe, Eastern Europe and Central Asia, North America, Latin America, and the rest of the world last
secs: Eastern Europe, the Caucasus & Central Asia
Middle East, Africa, South & Southeast Asia, Oceania

C14-5.label: Auteur Animated Short
C14-5.defn: An independent or state-studio art short driven by its maker's vision, the festival short of the European and world schools (Piccolo, Hedgehog in the Fog, The Street, Father and Daughter, The Windshield Wiper). American independents go to American Independent Animation; the National Film Board of Canada to its own leaf; stop-motion art shorts to C14-6.
C14-5.axis: by national school: the Zagreb School first, then the Polish School, the Czech-Hungarian-Bulgarian studios, the Soviet and post-Soviet schools, British, French-Belgian-Swiss and other Western European shorts, and the rest of the world last
secs: Italian, Iberian, German, Dutch & Nordic Shorts

new_leaves.label: American Independent Animation
new_leaves.breadth: US auteur shorts outside the studio system, from the underground to the festival circuit
new_leaves.defn: An auteur animated short made in the United States outside the studio system — the underground collage and experimental film, the independent studio short of the Hubleys and their circle, the art-school short, the web-era indie and the studio artist's personal festival short (Number 11: Mirror Animations, The Hole, Asparagus, Rejected, World of Tomorrow, Hair Love). Test: American production, an individual maker's vision; non-figurative work goes to C14-4, studio shorts to C14-3.
new_leaves.axis: by circle and era: underground and collage animation first, then the Hubleys and the independent studio short, the art-school and underground cartoon, Hertzfeldt and the web-era indies, and studio artists' personal festival shorts last

new_leaves.label: National Film Board of Canada Animation
new_leaves.breadth: auteur shorts of the NFB animation studios and the Canadian state-broadcaster tradition beside them
new_leaves.defn: An auteur animated short from the National Film Board of Canada's English and French animation studios, or from the Canadian public-broadcaster tradition around it (Neighbours, The Street, The Sweater, The Big Snit, The Man Who Planted Trees, When the Day Breaks). Test: a Canadian state-studio production; independents elsewhere stay in C14-5.

A16-13.label: Coming-of-Age Film
A16-13.defn: A drama of a child's or young adolescent's passage toward understanding, told from the child's side, in the ordinary settings of home, city or village (My Life as a Dog, The Long Day Closes, Boyhood, Ratcatcher, Close). Childhood under war or dictatorship goes to the War-Childhood Film; the summer away to the Summer Coming-of-Age Film; school and boarding school to the School Story Film; high-school teen life to A16-14; delinquency to A16-15.
A16-13.axis: by the setting of the childhood: home and family first, then city streets, and village and countryside last

new_leaves.label: War-Childhood Film
new_leaves.breadth: coming-of-age dramas of children under war, occupation or dictatorship
new_leaves.defn: A coming-of-age drama told from the side of a child growing up under war, occupation or dictatorship, where the historical violence shapes the passage (The Spirit of the Beehive, Cría Cuervos, In the Heat of the Sun, West Beirut, Kamchatka, Clandestine Childhood). Test: a child's-eye coming of age with war or repression as its condition; a combat film with child soldiers goes to A9.
new_leaves.aliases: childhood war film; children-in-war film; child's-eye war film

new_leaves.label: Summer Coming-of-Age Film
new_leaves.breadth: coming-of-age dramas of the summer holiday away from routine
new_leaves.defn: A coming-of-age drama set in the suspended time of a summer holiday — the trip, the camp, the summer house, the gang's adventure — whose end marks the passage (Stand by Me, My Father's Glory, The Sandlot, Summer 1993, The Way Way Back). Test: the summer away is the frame; school-year childhoods stay in A16-13.

new_leaves.label: School Story Film
new_leaves.breadth: childhood dramas set in the classroom or boarding school
new_leaves.defn: A childhood drama whose world is the school — the boarding school, the classroom and its teacher, exams and school tyranny — told from the pupils' side (Zéro de conduite, Evil, Son of Rambow, Our Twisted Hero, Playground, Monster). Test: pre-teen or early-adolescent pupils and their school; the high school goes to A16-14, college to A16-16, the teacher's own story to A16-17.

A13-22.label: Romantic Comedy-Drama
A13-22.defn: A romantic comedy played half-seriously, from the 1970s on, whose obstacle lies in the lovers' own eccentricity, damage, family burdens or age (Moonstruck, As Good as It Gets, Silver Linings Playbook, Something's Gotta Give, Amélie). The studio-era and other pre-1970 comedy-dramas go to the Classical Romantic Comedy-Drama; the American and English-language independent strand to the Indie Romantic Comedy; a purely dramatic treatment to A13-5.
A13-22.axis: by the lovers' burden: eccentricity, damage or illness, children and second chances, age, a homecoming

new_leaves.label: Classical Romantic Comedy-Drama
new_leaves.breadth: romantic comedy-dramas of the silent and studio eras, to 1969, across national cinemas
new_leaves.defn: A romantic comedy-drama of the silent and studio eras, before 1970, in any national cinema — the bittersweet star romance of Hollywood, the European and Soviet lyrical comedy, the Argentine and Mexican comedia romántica, the Asian and Egyptian studio romance (The Strawberry Blonde, Breakfast at Tiffany's, Walking the Streets of Moscow, Arroz con leche, Windfall in Athens). Test: made before 1970; screwball and sophisticated comedy go to their own leaves.
new_leaves.aliases: classical romantic comedy; studio-era romantic comedy
new_leaves.axis: by national studio tradition: Hollywood first, then Europe and the Soviet Union, Latin America, and Asia and the Middle East last

new_leaves.label: Indie Romantic Comedy
new_leaves.breadth: romantic comedy-dramas of the American and English-language independent cinema
new_leaves.defn: A romantic comedy-drama made in the American or English-language independent cinema from the 1970s on, deadpan, talky or wounded in tone and outside the studio formula (Minnie and Moskowitz, Chilly Scenes of Winter, Trust, Punch-Drunk Love, Results, The Big Sick, Enough Said). Test: independent production and an off-formula register; studio rom-coms of the same burdens stay in A13-22.
new_leaves.axis: by the lovers' burden: deadpan and eccentric lovers, then damaged and healing lovers, and age-gap love last
